title: Unequal batch sizes causing fairness and tail latency spikes — mitigation roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Investigation and remediation plan for recent production incidents where the continuous batcher formed strongly unequal sub-batches leading to prolonged GPU stalls, disproportionate tail latency for small requests, and apparent unfairness across customer traffic classes.
incident_summary: Between 2025-07-12 02:00 UTC and 2025-07-12 05:20 UTC several customer routes experienced sudden P95->P99 latency spikes despite overall throughput remaining in expected ranges. Correlated traces show batches containing a single large long-sequence request plus many small requests; the large request extended kernel runtime and prevented co-scheduled small requests from completing in their expected latency SLO window. Autoscale events and kernel-selection heuristics amplified the effect.
timeline: 2025-07-12 01:58 UTC: First alert on increased P99 for route /v1/generate-chat (internal alert threshold 4x baseline).
2025-07-12 02:05 UTC: On-call identifies batch composition skew; large sequence length >8k tokens co-scheduled with 1-2 token requests.
2025-07-12 02:20 UTC: Emergency throttle applied to large sequence requests as soft mitigation to reduce head-of-line blocking.
2025-07-12 03:10 UTC: Autoscaler triggered extra workers but kernel warmup + cache misses delayed benefit; tail remained high.
2025-07-12 04:00 UTC: Fairness probe added to runtime metrics; confirmed imbalance across customer tiers.
2025-07-12 05:30 UTC: Latency returned to baseline after aggressive request shaping and rollout of temporary per-slot size cap.
root_cause: A combination of factors: (1) continuous-batcher grouping heuristics prioritize fill-rate without accounting for extreme sequence-length variance, producing sub-batches where a single long request dominates GPU time; (2) kernel scheduling currently lacks preemption or sub-batch-aware time-slicing, so small requests wait for the long kernel to finish; (3) autoscaler and kernel-selection logic mispredicted memory residency and kernel runtime for mixed-length batches, delaying new capacity usefulness; (4) monitoring lacked an easy-to-query per-batch composition metric, delaying detection and automated mitigations.
mitigations: Immediate: Deploy per-slot max-token cap (soft) to prevent single-request domination; applied 2025-07-12 02:20 UTC.
Short-term (2 weeks): Adjust batcher heuristics to prefer homogeneous sequence-length grouping when variance > threshold; add fast-path that splits oversized requests into isolated micro-batches.
Medium-term (1-2 months): Implement aging-based fairness in scheduler (priority boost for requests waiting > X ms) and per-customer weight normalization to avoid starvation.
Medium-term: Enhance kernel-selection estimator to incorporate mixed-batch penalties and memory residency predictions so autoscaler decisions are more effective during mixed workloads.
Long-term (3+ months): Explore kernel preemption/time-slicing and model-execution checkpoints to allow co-scheduled small requests to make progress despite long-running kernels.
Monitoring: Add per-batch composition metrics (median/95th token length, largest-request fraction) and synthetic tests that simulate high-variance workloads for early detection.
